sentences.text:
Counsel for Applicant :- Anupam Tripathi Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.
Hon'ble Ajay Bhanot,J.
Matter is taken up in the revised call.

By means of the second bail application the applicant has prayed to be enlarged on bail in Case Crime No.96 of 2023 at Police Station-Mohammadabad, District-Farrukhabad under Sections 304B, 498A IPC and Sections 3/4 of D.P. Act.
The applicant is in jail since 31.05.2023.
The first bail application of the applicant was rejected by this Court on 25.10.2023.

The following arguments made by Shri Anupam Tripathi, learned counsel on behalf of the applicant,
which could not be satisfactorily refuted by Shri Chandan Agarwal, learned AGA-I from the record,
entitle the applicant for grant of bail:
Arun Kumar vs State Of U.P. on 10 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/121253182/
1 1.

sentences.text: The applicant is a law abiding citizen who cooperated with the police investigations and joined the trial proceedings.
He never influenced any witness nor did he tamper with the evidence.
2. The trial is moving at a snail's pace and shows no signs of an early conclusion.
The applicant is not responsible for the delay in the trial proceedings.

3. The status of the trial as referenced in the order dated 29.04.2024 passed by this Court while granting bail of a co-accused Kusama Devi registered as Criminal Misc.
Bail Application No. 16582 of 2024 records that as per charge-sheet, the prosecution proposes to examine 18 witnesses to bring home the charges.

entities.text:
Criminal Misc.
Bail Application No. 16582 of 2024
entities.label: CASE_NUMBER

sentences.text: However, 7 witnesses including the material witnesses namely, first informant-father of the victim, her brother, sister, uncle and sister-in-law have already been examined.
There is no possibility of the applicant influencing the said witnesses.
4. The prosecution witnesses have testified that the victim was suffering from epilepsy and was prone to bouts of uncontrollable rage and self harm.
5. Inordinate delay in concluding trial has lead to an indefinite detention of the applicant without there being any credible evidence to implicate him in the offence.
Right of the applicant to a speedy trial has been violated.

6. Continued incarceration of the applicant will disable him from crafting an effective defence strategy, gathering evidence in his support thereof and tendering the same before the learned trial court to absolve himself of the charges.
Any further incarceration would be to the detriment of the defence of the applicant and contrary to the norms of processual fairness in criminal jurisprudence.

7. This Court in Prabhat Gangwar v. State of U.P. (Criminal Misc. Bail Application No.2586 of 2023) while considering the grant of enlarging an accused on bail for preparing his defence and gathering evidence to tender the same before the learned trial court for establishing his innocence held:
"Nature and gravity of the offence is certainly liable to be considered by the court while considering grant of bail.

entities.text: Prabhat Gangwar v. State of U.P. (Criminal Misc. Bail Application No.2586 of 2023)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The Court has also to factor the likelihood of whether the accused committed the offence while deciding a bail application.

The court also has to determine in the facts of the case whether the accused needs to be set at liberty to frame his defence and gather evidence to refute the prosecution case and establish his innocence.
The bail court has to examine whether continued incarceration would disable the accused from tendering an effective defence of his case.
This is a demand of processual fairness in criminal jurisprudence.
Setting an accused at liberty at large on this ground cannot be applied mechanically in all cases.

The issue has to be considered in the facts and circumstances of each case Arun Kumar vs State Of U.P. on 10 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/121253182/
2

entities.text: Arun Kumar vs State Of U.P.
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: while doing so

. All relevant facts including the evidences in the record, the conduct of the accused during the investigation as well as trial have to be adverted to before a decision is made in this regard."
8. Considering the aforesaid parameters in light of the above facts of this case
, I am of the opinion that Prabhat Gangwar (supra) is applicable to the facts of this case.

9. The applicant claims congruency in role and seeks parity in relief granted to the co-accused who has been enlarged on bail by this Court by order dated 29.04.2024 in Criminal Misc. Bail Application No. 16582 of 2024.
10.

entities.text: Criminal Misc. Bail Application No. 16582 of 2024
entities.label: CASE_NUMBER

sentences.text: The applicant does not have any criminal history apart from the instant case.
11. The applicant is not a flight risk.
The applicant being a law abiding citizen has always cooperated with the investigation and undertakes to join the trial proceedings.
There is no possibility of his influencing witnesses, tampering with the evidence or reoffending.
In the light of the preceding discussion and without making any observations on the merits of the case, the bail application is allowed.
Let the applicant-Arun Kumar be released on bail in the aforesaid case crime number, on furnishing a personal bond and two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the court below.

The following conditions be imposed in the interest of justice:-
(i) The applicant will not tamper with the evidence or influence any witness during the trial.
(ii) The applicant will appear before the trial court on the date fixed, unless personal presence is exempted.

The learned trial court is directed to fix the sureties after due application of mind in light of the judgement rendered by this Court in Arvind Singh v. State of U.P. Thru. Prin. Secy. Home Deptt.
(Application U/S 482 No.2613 of 2023).

sentences.text: The learned trial court shall ensure that the right of bail of the applicant granted by this Court is not frustrated by arbitrary demands of sureties or onerous conditions which are unrelated to the socioeconomic status of the applicant.

Learned District Judge, Farrukhabad is directed to comply with the order dated 29.04.2024 passed by this Court in Criminal Misc. Bail Application No.16582 of 2023 (Kusama Devi v. State of U.P.).
It is further directed that in case the applicant or any accused person who has been enlarged on bail does not cooperate in the trial or adopts dilatory tactics, the learned trial court shall record a finding to this effect and cancel the bail without recourse to this Court.
